history.dynasty: None (managed by the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee - modern institution; one source claims 1737 renovation by Baba Ala Singh, founder of Patiala - verify)
history.period: Early 18th century - Guru Gobind Singh's visit on 14 Poh 1761 Bikrami (December 1704); present six-storied gurdwara building modern
history.summary: THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE. Gurdwara Sri Manji Sahib (Alamgir Sahib) stands in Alamgir village, about 11 km south of Ludhiana on the Ludhiana-Malerkotla highway - NOT in Ludhiana city itself. It commemorates Guru Gobind Singh Ji's stay here after the martyrdom of his four sons (the Sahibzadas) and his mother at Sirhind. Travelling in disguise as 'Uchh Da Pir' (a high priest of Uch), carried on a bed by Bhai Daya Singh, Bhai Dharam Singh, Bhai Man Singh and the Pathan brothers Nabi Khan and Gani Khan, he reached Alamgir from Machhiwara on 14 Poh 1761 Bikrami (December 1704) and rested here for three days. Tradition holds that the Guru shot an arrow that killed a python in a well (giving it mukti), then struck the ground again to raise a fresh spring - the Tirsar (arrow-lake) Sarovar; a leprous old woman bathing in it was healed. The horse-trader Bhai Nigahia Singh gifted the Guru a horse here (one account says Bhai Naudha), and the Guru sent Nabi Khan and Gani Khan back with a hukamnama honouring their service. The gurdwara stands where the Guru's bed was set down. An annual three-day fair is held here in December (verify dates). The claim on one travel site that the shrine was 'established in 1660 by Guru Gobind Singh' and 'dedicated to Guru Tegh Bahadur' contradicts the established 1704 visit account and should not be repeated.

name: Gurdwara Sri Manji Sahib (Alamgir Sahib)
town_description: Alamgir is a village in Ludhiana district, Punjab (PIN 141116), about 11 km south of Ludhiana city on the Ludhiana-Malerkotla highway. It is dominated by the historic Gurdwara Sri Manji Sahib complex with its Tirsar Sarovar, and is one of the most frequently visited Sikh shrines in Ludhiana district.

travel.airport: Sahnewal Airport (Ludhiana) has limited service (verify); nearest major airport is Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~135 km) or Chandigarh (~100 km).
travel.railway: Ludhiana Junction is 11-16 km away depending on the listing (verify); taxis and autos to Alamgir via the Malerkotla road.
travel.road: On the Ludhiana-Malerkotla highway, ~11 km south of Ludhiana; reached by city buses, autos and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; the December 3-day fair is the peak event (crowded).
visitor_information.opening_hours: No fixed hours published on the official district page (verify); gurdwaras typically open from early morning till night. Langar is served; cover your head and remove shoes before entering.
